main_text.p: partes sunt, sed quatenus organicæ, & instrumentales, aut mistam edunt actionem. Id autem, quòd postea Fernelius producit ex Galeni sententia, & authoritate, nimirum partis substantiam ad robur non parū conferre, nō satis probat materiam per se nonnullis subijci morbis, forma salua & tempe ramento. Nam hoc loco substantia pro materia sumi, non est verisimile, quandoquidem per se nihil agit materia, sed est dunta xat passionis causa. Immaterialia enim nihil pati queunt. At id robur efflagitat, quòd agendi uim habet. Quare substantia hic sumitur pro corpore similaris partis, quod quidem edit actionem. Quamuis etiam ad partis similaris substantiam robur pertineat, ipsum tamen à solo temperamento proficisci testantur Hippocrates, Galenus, & cæteri præclariores medici. Adde quòd omnis partium similarium imbecillitas, quæ robori opponitur, ab aliqua intemperie semper prouenit, quemadmodum iam ostendimus. Quod ibidem his subiungit Fernelius, nempe spiritus, carnis, & solidarum partium substantiam esse materiam, ex qua quælibet similaris pars nostri corporis est conflata: à veterum dogmate omnino alienum videtur.

page.notes: Transcription is a faithful reading of the printed text, with the long s normalised to s and the u/v and i/j spelling adjusted. Some words are uncertain and should be checked against the scan: "dunta" (line about "est dunta xat passionis") is probably a printing error for "duntaxat"; I have kept it as printed. The phrase "quæ robori" and "substantia hic sumitur" are clear. The printed "Quod ibidem his subiungit" and "nempe spiritus" are read as printed. Some letters near the ink-damaged edges, especially in "intemperie" and "est verisimile", should be verified. Marginal notes: none printed on this page. The reference mark "y" is not present. Printing errors left as printed: "dunta", "semper prouenit", and the words "partes sunt" are as they appear. Text below the column: none.
